public_rationale: Read plainly, he says generative AI had not created meaningful numbers of new jobs in the 18 months before July 2024. Indeed Hiring Lab found GenAI-related postings grew more than 30-fold from January 2023, and its economists said GenAI was 'already creating new jobs'. But the same data put those postings at about 11 in 10,000, 'a very small share' of US jobs. They also do not show the roles were net new rather than existing jobs that now mention GenAI. OpenAI had about 1,200 staff, but one firm's hiring is not economy-wide job creation. Without a measure of net new jobs, and with no threshold in his words, the evidence neither confirms nor refutes the claim.
limitations: Posting shares are not employment counts.
Data come from one job board, Indeed.
A literal 'zero new jobs' reading would be contradicted by e2, but that reading stretches his words against him.

criteria.contradiction_condition: Labour-market data for 2023 to mid-2024 showing a material number of new jobs created because of generative AI, beyond relabelled existing roles, at a scale an informed reader would call meaningful.
